Acer Inc. (2353) \u2019s new Iconia 6120 Touchbook has many of the\nfeatures you would expect from a full-sized laptop: an  Intel\nCorp. (INTC)  i5 microprocessor,  Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) \u2019s Windows 7 operating\nsystem, a 14-inch display.  It\u2019s also missing one feature you would expect: a keyboard.\nIn its place is a second 14-inch touch screen. Need to type\nsomething? A full-sized virtual keyboard, complete with\ntouchpad, appears on the bottom display when you lay your palms\non it, to be used and then dismissed when no longer required.  Think of the Iconia Touchbook as a Windows PC for the iPad\ngeneration, for whom having to type on glass is a feature and\nnot a flaw.  The dual-screen approach isn\u2019t original with Acer;  Toshiba\nCorp. (6502)  did something similar with its Libretto last year. The\nLibretto, though, was a limited-edition concept PC with much\nsmaller screens than those on the Acer. While the Iconia lacks a\nDVD or CD drive, it\u2019s otherwise the antithesis of an under-\nequipped, lightweight netbook.  The computer, which is  available for order  now and shows up\nin stores later this month, costs $1,199.99. It weighs a hefty\n6.2 pounds, and comes with 4 gigabytes of memory and a 640-\ngigabyte hard drive standard. It also has a webcam, high-\ndefinition video and audio connections and three USB ports, one\nof them the new, ultra-fast USB 3.0.  A Choice of Control  The  Iconia \u2019s upper screen, like the lower one, is touch-\nenabled, giving you the choice of controlling your Windows\napplications from the virtual touchpad on the bottom screen, or\ndirectly with your finger, similar to Apple\u2019s iPad. If you\u2019re in\ndirect-control mode, you can drag windows from one screen to the\nother, or even expand them to fill both.  A number of the computer\u2019s functions and settings can be\naccessed via the Acer Ring, a sort of virtual dial you can\nsummon on the lower screen. Here you\u2019ll find controls for video,\nphoto and music applications as well as the Gesture Editor,\nwhich lets you design your own set of taps and swipes to start\nprograms or perform other tasks.  Typing on the glass takes some getting used to, though it\nwasn\u2019t nearly as difficult as I had expected. I could adjust the\nsize of the function keys, and by angling the screen was able to\nfind comfortable typing positions in a variety of situations. My\nbiggest problem wasn\u2019t with the keyboard but with the trackpad,\nwhich is so small that my finger kept sliding past its virtual\nedges.  Keys and Clicks  While there\u2019s no tactile feedback when you land on a\nvirtual key, as there is on some smartphones, you can hear an\naudible \u201cclick.\u201d It\u2019s a nice idea, except that there is a\nnoticeable lag between hitting the key and hearing the sound.  Other features designed to make things easier fall short as\nwell. While you can enter text with your finger or a stylus via\na handwriting-recognition window, the process is laborious. And\n Nuance Communications Inc. (NUAN) \u2019s included predictive-text software,\nwhich came enabled by default, annoyingly kept trying to\n\u201ccorrect\u201d the spelling of my passwords and the capitalization\nof words I wanted to be uppercase. I quickly turned it off.  Power Drain  The biggest drawback is the battery. The two touch screens\nsuck power like a vacuum cleaner, and even Acer\u2019s claim of three\nhours on a full charge may be on the high side if you\u2019ve got the\nscreens set to bright and are connected to a Wi-Fi network.\nMoreover, the battery isn\u2019t user-replaceable, so you\u2019ll tend to\nfind yourself tethered to an electrical outlet.  Like many PC-makers, Acer is groping to find its way in a\nmarket increasingly moving toward tablets and other mobile\ndevices; its chief executive officer, Gianfranco Lanci, resigned\nlast week in a rift with the board over strategy.  With the Iconia Touchbook, Acer at the very least deserves\ncredit for doing something unusual in the well-ordered if ho-hum\nworld of Windows computing, and a certain sort of user may find\nthe laptop\u2019s technology-forward approach irresistible.  Most people, though, will probably conclude it is a little\ntoo out there, and too hampered by its heft and battery-life\nissues. If it\u2019s possible to be a really cool failure, this one\nis. While Slim, 73, is best known as the majority owner of embattled wireless carrier  America Movil (AMXL)  SAB, his banking, mining and construction companies are so expensive that if they aligned with industry averages, he would relinquish the mantle to Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates.  The Mexican billionaire\u2019s bank, Grupo Financiero  Inbursa (GFINBURO)  SAB, is trading at 26.1 times trailing earnings, the highest among five publicly-traded Mexican lenders, whose average valuation is 20.2 times earnings, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Minera Frisco (MFRISCOA)  SAB, the mining company, and Inbursa have the first and third lowest ratings among 58 Mexican stocks tracked by three or more equity analysts, with most of Wall Street recommending selling the shares. Lawmakers are considering legislation that would create an agency with power to regulate competition and could force companies to sell assets.  America Movil, Latin America\u2019s biggest wireless carrier, has  tumbled  13 percent since the bill was unveiled March 11. The company accounts for $31.3 billion of his fortune, while Inbursa, holding company Grupo Carso SAB and Minera Frisco accounted for another $10 billion, $9.2 billion and $8.7 billion of his wealth, respectively. Roberto Cavazos, a money manager with Value Casa de Bolsa SA, said Slim companies deserve a premium over their peers because of his record of generating profits for shareholders and maintaining sound balance sheets.  Inbursa has a capitalization index of 19.9 percent, compared with about 13.2 percent for peer Grupo Financiero Banorte SAB, according to data compiled by the National Banking and Securities Commission. The capitalization index expresses net capital as a portion of total risk-weighted assets. Trademark  Facebook Trial Over \u2018Timeline\u2019 Trademark Rights Postponed  Facebook  Inc.\u2019s trial over its right to use the word\n\u201ctimeline\u201d to describe user profiles has been delayed at least\na day and possibly longer.  A  jury trial  in the trademark infringement case filed in\n2011 by the operator of  timelines.com  was scheduled to start\nyesterday at the federal courthouse in  Chicago .  More than 90 minutes after conferring with lawyers and\ndeclaring a recess, U.S. District Judge John W. Facebook is the world\u2019s most-popular social networking\nwebsite. The  Menlo Park , California-based company has more than\na billion monthly users, according to its website.  Timelines\u2019 website allows its users to create or add\ncontent to historical chronologies documenting topics including\nspace exploration, political assassinations, wars and sporting\nevents.  Chicago-based Timelines sued Facebook a week after the\nsocial network announced it was converting user-profile pages\npreviously known as walls to individual chronologies called\ntimelines.  The website Timelines, which has about 94,000 visitors a\nmonth, contends it has held a U.S. trademark on the use of\n\u201ctimelines\u201d for user-created Internet chronologies since 2009.  The company is seeking an order barring Facebook from using\nthe word, according to its amended complaint. The  California  company has also countersued, claiming the\ntrademark is too generic to warrant federal rights protection.\nDarrah on April 1 denied a defense motion for judgment on the\nissue, setting the matter for a jury trial.  The case is Timelines Inc. v.  Facebook Inc. (FB) , 11-cv-06867,\nU.S. District Court, Northern District of  Illinois  (Chicago). Copyright  Astrolabe Backs Down from Copyright Claims Against Scientists  Astrolabe Inc.  a maker of astrology software programs, has\nwithdrawn the copyright-infringement suit it filed against two\ncomputer scientists.  The Brewster, Massachusetts-based company sued Arthur David\nOlson of the National Institutes of Health\u2019s National Cancer\nInstitute and Paul R. Eggert of the Computer Science Department\nof the University of  California ,  Los Angeles  in federal court in\nBoston Sept. 30.  The two computer scientists were accused of infringing the\ncopyright for an atlas containing historical time zone\ninformation. Astrolabe objects to the scientists\u2019 websites\npublication of time zone data.  Astrolabe asked the court to order the two scientists to\nhalt their alleged infringement, and for awards of money\ndamages, attorney fees and litigation costs. Astrolabe bases its\nclaims on its ownership of the \u201cACS International Atlas,\u201d the\n\u201cACS American Atlas,\u201d and related software programs and\ndatabases.  The case has attracted the interest of the scientific and\ntechnology community because the data is used in Unix and Linux\nplatforms to set clocks and for time-zone updates. In  a posting\nto a technology interest-group mailing list , Olson said the\nserver that provides these updates has been shut down in\nresponse to the suit.  Stephen Colebourne, a developer who works with Java\nprograms in the U.K., had said  in a blog posting  that the result\nof the takedown was that \u201cthere is no longer a single central\nlocation for time-zone information for computing.\u201d  In a notice posted on its website Jan. 12, San Francisco-\nbased  Electronic Frontier Foundation  called the suit \u201cbogus,\u201d\nsaying that facts aren\u2019t copyright protectable.  Noting that Olson took the updates offline, EFF said the\ncase \u201cwould be laughable but for the dangerous consequence\u201d\nand noted the \u201cshock and dismay of the many users and\ndevelopers who relied upon the updates.\u201d  Although EFF said it would file a motion seeking sanctions\nagainst Astrolabe, that motion was never filed, according to\ndata compiled by Bloomberg.  In a Feb. 22 filing, Astrolabe has agreed to dismiss the\ncase. The two defendants hadn\u2019t answered the complaint or filed\na motion to have the case dismissed.  The scientists were represented by  Adam J. Kessel  and\n Olivia T. Nguyen  of  Fish & Richardson PC (1357L)  and  Corynne McSherry \nand  Mitchell L. Tech stocks capped their best 10 weeks of relative\nperformance since 2009 last week, and the Guggenheim Standard &\nPoor\u2019s 500 Equal-Weight Technology exchange-traded fund has\noutpaced the  Guggenheim S&P 500 Equal-Weight ETF (RSP)  by 4.8\npercentage points since April 19. The gains show a \u201chand off\u201d\nis starting, as investors move into industries that could\noutperform benchmarks later in the economic expansion, said\nBrian Jacobsen, who helps oversee $221.2 billion as chief\nportfolio strategist at Wells Fargo Advantage Funds in Menomonee\nFalls,  Wisconsin .  \u201cIf the Fed is confident enough to begin taking the\ntraining wheels off the economy, then that should benefit tech\nstocks,\u201d he said. Wells Fargo maintains an overweight\nrecommendation on the sector partly because capital spending on\nthese products would improve with increased assurance about the\ndurability of the expansion, he said.  The Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco\u2019s Tech Pulse\nIndex, which tracks the health of the U.S. information-technology industry, is showing an improvement in investment,\nconsumption, employment, industrial production and shipments.\nThe index rose to 98.96 in May, the highest since 2008.  Unprecedented Stimulus  The equal-weight technology ETF began to lead the benchmark\nindex shortly before the Fed started bracing investors for a\nphase-out of its unprecedented monetary-stimulus program. At the\nconclusion of a two-day meeting May 1, the Federal Open Market\nCommittee said it was \u201cprepared to increase or reduce the pace\nof its purchases to maintain appropriate policy accommodation as\nthe outlook for the labor market or inflation changes.\u201d  Chairman Ben S. Bernanke provided more detail on June 19\nwhen he said the central bank may begin to taper its $85 billion\nin monthly bond buying later this year and halt purchases in\nmid-2014 as long as the world\u2019s largest economy performs in line\nwith its projections.  Officials  project  the U.S. will expand 3 percent to 3.5\npercent in the fourth quarter of 2014 from the same period this\nyear, according to their central-tendency estimate, which\nexcludes the three highest and three lowest estimates. The March\nprojection was a range of 2.9 percent to 3.4 percent.  U.S. Growth  Gross domestic product grew at a 1.8 percent annualized\nrate in the first quarter, revised from a prior reading of 2.4\npercent, Commerce Department data show.  As the expansion enters its fifth year, there are signs it\nis \u201ccloser to being self-sustaining,\u201d which is helping to\nspark interest in technology stocks because these companies\u2019\nearnings are cyclical and benefit from an improving economy,\nsaid David Katz, who oversees about $850 million as chief\ninvestment officer at New York-based Matrix Asset Advisors Inc.\n\u201cOver the next six to 12 months, tech is going to be a good\nplace to invest.\u201d  Shares of  Cisco Systems Inc. (CSCO) ,  Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) ,  Hewlett-Packard Co. (HPQ)  and  TE Connectivity Ltd. (TEL)  \u201chave done well and are\npoised to do better\u201d as demand improves, Katz said. (DATA)  offer\n\u201cinteresting\u201d opportunities with \u201crevenue that\u2019s growing like\na weed,\u201d said Erick Maronak, chief investment officer at\nVictory Capital Management Inc. in New York, which oversees $28\nbillion.  \u2018Favorite\u2019 Stocks  Tech stocks now are JPMorgan Chase & Co.\u2019s \u201cfavorite\u201d\nbecause they offer a \u201cbeta play on growth\u201d and attractive\nfundamentals, said Thomas Lee, the bank\u2019s chief U.S. equity\nstrategist in New York. \u201cInvestors haven\u2019t been that excited\nabout this group,\u201d though sentiment has been improving as the\nprospect of changing Fed policy encourages some repositioning,\nhe said. A stock with a high beta tends to rise or fall more\nthan the broader market.  The equal-weight technology ETF reduces the influence of\nany one \u201coversized\u201d company, and while \u201ceverybody talks about\nthe big-cap names,\u201d small-cap companies also offer an\ninteresting investment opportunity, Jacobsen said.  Small-cap tech stocks capped their best 10 weeks since 2011\nlast week, and the Russell 2000 Technology Index has outpaced\nthe Russell 2000 Index by 6.9 percentage points since April 19.\nThe relative performance of both the equal-weighted and small-cap groups shows that \u201cinvestors have more conviction\u201d in this\nindustry now, said Jim Stellakis, founder and director of\nresearch at Greenwich, Connecticut-based research company\nTechnical Alpha Inc. and a chartered market technician.  Clear Sign  If these indexes were to trade above highs set in August\n2012 relative to the market, this would be \u201ca clear sign that\ninvestors are more comfortable overweighting this sector as\ntheir expectations for earnings are improving,\u201d Stellakis said.\nAnother \u201cbullish signal\u201d is that the equal-weight ETF\n\u201creversed all of its relative weakness and ended up\noutperforming the market on June 28,\u201d he said, even as shares\nof  Accenture Plc (ACN)  tumbled  10 percent  to $71.96 that day, the\nbiggest decline since August 2011.  The world\u2019s second-largest technology-consulting company\nand a member of the equal-weight ETF said June 27 that fiscal\nfourth-quarter revenue will be $6.7 billion to $7 billion,\nfalling short of the $7.36 billion average estimate of analysts,\naccording to data compiled by Bloomberg.  Less Leveraged  Higher interest rates historically bode well for tech\nstocks, as they tend to lead the broader market during periods\nof rising short-term yields, Jacobsen said. That\u2019s in part\nbecause these companies are less financially leveraged than\npeers in other industries, so they\u2019re \u201cnot as vulnerable\u201d to\nhigher costs for servicing debt, Lee said. That\u2019s unusual\nbecause tech usually trades at a premium to the broader market,\nhe said. (AAPL)  Chief Executive Officer  Tim Cook  apologized for the iPhone mapping software released last week that has been criticized for flaws such as misrouted directions and inaccurately located landmarks.  \u201cWe are extremely sorry for the frustration this has caused our customers and we are doing everything we can to make Maps better,\u201d Cook said in a  letter  to customers posted today on the Cupertino, California-based company\u2019s website.  Apple\u2019s decision to build its navigation application reflects a widening rift with  Google Inc. (GOOG) , which had provided its  Google Maps  program since the iPhone debuted in 2007. While the new software adds features such as turn-by-turn navigation, it is widely faulted for unreliable landmark searches, routes that get users lost and a lack of public transit directions.  \u201cAn apology is never bad,\u201d  Carl Howe , an analyst at  Yankee Group  in  Boston , said in an interview. \u201cBut notice they didn\u2019t say that they are going to reinstate Google Maps. There is no impact, there is no change in philosophy or direction.\u201d  Apple\u2019s mapping application was released as part of the new iOS 6 software, which runs the iPhone, iPad and iPod Touch. Cook said that the feature will improve as the company collects more data. In the meantime, he said people who are frustrated with the experience could download mapping applications such as Microsoft Corp.\u2019s Bing, Waze and MapQuest from the company\u2019s  App Store . He said customers also could use the iPhone\u2019s Internet browser to use Google\u2019s mapping application.  \u2018Their Call\u2019  Google Chairman  Eric Schmidt  said on Sept. 25 that Apple should have stuck with Google Maps. \u201cIt would have been better if they had kept ours,\u201d Schmidt said at a press event in  Tokyo . \u201cWhat were we going to do, force them not to change their mind? It\u2019s their call.\u201d  Nate Tyler, a spokesman for Google, declined to comment beyond an online post explaining how to access its maps through the iPhone Web browser. The company hasn\u2019t submitted a mapping app to Apple for the approval needed for it to appear in the App Store, a person familiar with the matter said on Sept. 25.  Google has been building out its online mapping software since  2005 , using cars and satellites to accumulate data that helps improve its accuracy and reliability. To catch up, Apple can use location data collected from customers using its maps to improve the service. Apple\u2019s map software includes a feedback feature for users to report inaccurate directions and other bugs.  \u2018Fell Short\u2019  \u201cAt Apple, we strive to make world-class products that deliver the best experience possible to our customers,\u201d Cook said. \u201cWith the launch of our new Maps last week, we fell short on this commitment.\u201d  In the past few years, Apple has  acquired  small mapping companies including C3 Technologies, Poly9 and Placebase. The location information that Apple licenses from  TomTom NV (TOM2)  and OpenStreetMap isn\u2019t as good as Google, said Noam Bardin, the CEO of Waze Inc., which makes an iPhone mapping app.  \u201cThe big problem is they\u2019re 100 percent hostage to the quality of their data -- Apple is stuck,\u201d Bardin said. While the quality will improve, it will be very expensive to match the billions Google has already spent on maps, he said. \u201cThe tactical challenge is they bit off what Google does really well and tried to do it themselves.\u201d  Record Sales  Apple had to have known the application had problems during the testing period and decided to move ahead nonetheless, Bardin said.  The mapping fiasco is a product of Apple\u2019s growing rivalry with Google, the maker of the world\u2019s most popular smartphone software. Google\u2019s Android operating system runs on devices from manufacturers including Samsung Electronics Co. and  HTC Corp. (2498)  that compete with the iPhone.  Apple built the replacement app because it wanted to scale back its relationship with Google, not because of any glaring product flaws, two people familiar with Apple\u2019s development of the mapping features said last week.  The feud also extends beyond maps. For the first time since 2007, Google\u2019s YouTube video service isn\u2019t preinstalled on the new iPhone. Schmidt exited Apple\u2019s board of directors in 2009 as tensions escalated between the competitors.  Apple took a strategic risk releasing its own maps app before it was ready, said Barbara Kahn, a marketing professor at the Wharton School at the  University of Pennsylvania .  \u2018Competitor\u2019s Brand\u2019  \u201cMaps is a very critical Google brand,\u201d Kahn said in an interview. \u201cApple doesn\u2019t want their competitor\u2019s brand all over their phone.\u201d  That said, defects with the maps isn\u2019t likely to crimp sales of the iPhone 5, said  Gene Munster , an analyst at Piper Jaffray Cos. Apple sold a record 5 million iPhone 5s during the handset\u2019s debut weekend. The device, which has a bigger screen and is lighter than previous models, went on sale in another 22 countries today and will be in 100 by the end of the year.  \u201cConsumer sentiment on the iPhone remains high,\u201d Munster wrote in a research note today. \u201cThe maps product is not causing a user backlash.\u201d  The maps software joins a list of other faulty services Apple has introduced in recent years. It recently discontinued the Ping music social network after it failed to attract users. MobileMe, a product for e-mail, calender and other online services, was also plagued by defects and recently transitioned into Apple\u2019s iCloud service.  Prior Apologies  This is also the third time Apple has had to apologize or reverse course during the introduction of a new iPhone.  Following the first iPhone release in 2007, Apple co- founder  Steve Jobs  offered users rebates and an  apology  because early customers complained about a price cut two months after it went on sale.  In 2010, Jobs apologized and gave out free cases to customers because of antenna defects for the iPhone 4. After  Consumer Reports  and other publications showed the device would lose its signal if held a certain way, Jobs called a rare press conference to explain the issue.  The mapping application has made the company a target of ridicule. A  website  was created to chronicle various snafus, including one where a huge swath of Portland, Oregon, is shown as a park and others where bridges are labeled as being on land. In one  New York  example, Lexington Ave. is listed as being in Brooklyn, not  Manhattan .  \u201cMaps is an appalling first release,\u201d  David Pogue , the technology critic for the New York Times, said in a review this week. \u201cIt may be the most embarrassing, least usable piece of software Apple has ever unleashed.\u201d  Apple fell 2.1 percent to $667.11 at the close in New York, paring the gain for the year to 65 percent. Regional and rural wireless providers are backing several\nbills in Congress that would let consumers unlock mobile phones\nand tablet computers without carriers\u2019 permission. Big phone\ncompanies often land exclusive rights to offer the hottest\ndevices, and U.S. rules currently prohibit altering software to\nlet new phones from one carrier to work on other networks.  \u201cSmaller carriers have a very difficult time getting\naccess to smartphones and handsets,\u201d said  Steven Berry ,\npresident of the Competitive Carriers Association, which\nrepresents such companies as  U.S. Cellular Corp. (T) , barring consumers from unlocking their handsets\nwithout their carrier\u2019s approval. The rules change, which took\neffect Jan. 26, reversed an earlier exemption under copyright\nlaw.  The Library of Congress\u2019s Copyright Office, as part of a\nperiodic review, said changing software to let one carrier\u2019s\nphones work on other networks wasn\u2019t among activities expressly\npermitted under copyright law.  CTIA-The Wireless Association, with members including\nVerizon, AT&T,  Sprint Nextel Corp. President  Barack Obama \u2019s administration said March 4 that\nconsumers should be allowed to unlock smartphones and tablet\ncomputers without risking criminal penalties, citing a White\nHouse online petition endorsed by more than 114,000 people.  Handset makers and big-box retailers such as  Best Buy Co. (BBY) \nhave begun selling unlocked devices that work with multiple\ncarriers. Creating a Report  When a client puts an address into EagleView\u2019s website, the\ncompany pulls existing aerial photos of that property. (MSFT)  Chief Executive Officer Steve Ballmer, who has struggled to adapt the world\u2019s largest software maker to the shift away from personal computers and toward mobile devices, will retire after more than a decade at the helm.  Ballmer, 57, plans to step down within 12 months, Redmond, Washington-based Microsoft said today in a statement. The company\u2019s lead independent director,  John Thompson , will oversee the search for his successor, heading a committee that will also include Microsoft co-founder  Bill Gates . Investors applauded the move, sending the shares up the most since 2009.  Ballmer\u2019s move reflects the changes roiling the computing industry his company helped pioneer. Microsoft, which supplies the software running most PCs, lost almost half its value on Ballmer\u2019s watch. The stock hasn\u2019t closed above $50 since his first year on the job amid competition from  Google Inc. (GOOG) ,  Apple Inc. (AAPL)  and  Facebook Inc. (FB)  in everything from tablets to the Web.  Related Features: \u201cThere is never a perfect time for this type of transition, but now is the right time,\u201d Ballmer wrote in a  memo  to employees today that was posted on Microsoft\u2019s website. \u201cWe need a CEO who will be here longer term for this new direction.\u201d  Management Reorganization  The announcement comes six weeks after Ballmer streamlined the company\u2019s management, spurring speculation that he was grooming successors. He cut the number of business units to four and said Windows chief Julie Larson-Green, 51, would oversee all hardware, including the Surface tablet and Xbox console and related games. Windows Phone software head Terry Myerson gained responsibility for the Windows and Xbox operating systems. Skype president Tony Bates, 46, was put in charge of a new group for business development and acquisitions.  Other PC-related companies have also been struggling with the decline in their industry.  Intel Corp. (INTC) , which supplies the chips used in PCs, announced a CEO change last year.  Dell Inc. (DELL) , the No. 3 PC maker, is embroiled in a months-long battle to go private. And this week,  Hewlett-Packard Co. (HPQ) , the No. 2 PC company, shook up its executive ranks as it attempts a turnaround.  The mantle of technology leadership has instead been taken up by Google, Apple and Facebook, which have over the past decade moved the landscape toward trends like mobile, search and social networking -- all areas where Microsoft is weak.  Challenged Business  Amid these shifts, Microsoft last month reported quarterly profit and sales that missed analysts\u2019 estimates. The company\u2019s latest computing operating system, Windows 8, also hasn\u2019t spurred the comeback that Ballmer was aiming for. In April, activist investor ValueAct Holdings LP disclosed a stake of about $1.9 billion in Microsoft, pushing the software maker to consider giving the shareholder a board seat.  \u201cHe\u2019s become a lightning rod for frustration over Microsoft\u2019s lack of progress in mobile and Windows 8,\u201d said  Richard Williams , an analyst at Cross Research in Millburn,  New Jersey .  The company\u2019s stock rose 7.3 percent to $34.75 at the close in  New York .  Ballmer had thought about retirement for quite a while and the timing became clearer over the last few months, he said in an  interview  with ZDNet. The CEO said he officially decided that he would exit during a board call two days ago. Gates, who is chairman and on the board, didn\u2019t ask Ballmer to stay, said the CEO.  Internal Shock  \u201cBill respects my decision,\u201d Ballmer said to ZDNet. \u201cUltimately, these kinds of things have to be one\u2019s own personal decision.\u201d  Members of Microsoft\u2019s senior leadership team only learned about Ballmer\u2019s decision to retire last night, said a person with knowledge of the matter. Many senior executives were surprised, said the person, who asked not to be identified because the discussions were private.  Microsoft said it would consider both external and internal candidates for CEO. Among the internal candidates are Bates, Myerson, Satya Nadella, head of the server business who was appointed to direct cloud and enterprise products last month, and Qi Lu, responsible for the Bing search engine and other Internet projects and who was named to oversee Office and the Skype videoconference business and to run a new applications group, according to people with knowledge of the matter who asked not to identified because the discussions are private.  Someone who isn\u2019t in the running is Gates, 57, who has been working on projects at the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, among other things, said two people with knowledge of the matter.  Ballmer-Gates Relationship  Ballmer took over the CEO role in 2000 from Gates, his schoolmate at  Harvard University . While Ballmer had a boisterous style that made him legendary at company presentations, he largely remained in Gates\u2019s shadow. Ballmer wasn\u2019t seen as possessing the same vision for technology or the ability to anticipate changes in the industry, said Williams.  \u201cBallmer was more the executive than the visionary and he missed a few turning points that visionaries wouldn\u2019t have,\u201d Williams said.  Unlike Gates, who dropped out of Harvard to start Microsoft, Ballmer stayed in school and received a degree in applied math and economics. He then joined Microsoft in 1980.  Gates and Ballmer had very different management styles. While Gates was Microsoft\u2019s geeky visionary, Ballmer was its excitable salesman. One video of the CEO on YouTube, entitled \u201cThe Best of  Steve Ballmer ,\u201d features clips of him yelping and jumping on stage, wide-eyed and sweating, singing Microsoft\u2019s virtues.  Microsoft\u2019s Rise  In the 1980s and 90s, Microsoft\u2019s swift rise to PC software dominance made Ballmer a billionaire many times over. He is the world\u2019s 44th richest person, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, with a fortune of $16.8 billion. Gates, the richest person in the world, has a net worth of $72.4 billion.  \u201cThis is a time of important transformation for Microsoft,\u201d Ballmer wrote in the memo. \u201cThis is an emotional and difficult thing for me to do. I take this step in the best interests of the company I love.\u201d  He said he plans to continue as one of the company\u2019s largest owners. Ballmer is the company\u2019s No. 5 shareholder, with a 4 percent stake, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.  With Microsoft shares soaring today on the announcement of his coming retirement, Ballmer\u2019s net worth jumped about $786 million, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.  Big Shakeup  Last month\u2019s reorganization, Microsoft\u2019s largest shakeup in a decade, is designed to speed development of hardware and services as the company\u2019s Windows business suffers from the shrinking PC market and poor demand for Windows-based mobile devices. The shuffle reversed some changes Ballmer made in 2002, when he divided Microsoft into what was then seven individual product units, each led by an executive with operational and financial responsibilities.  In the decade since then, he mainly tinkered with individual businesses. In 2011, Bob Muglia was pushed out as server chief, and in 2006 Ballmer revamped leadership of the Windows and Internet units after development delays for the Windows Vista operating system.  The latest reorganization was seen by analysts as a signal of which executives may be poised to succeed Ballmer. Before taking charge of hardware, Larson-Green helped spearhead a radical redesign of Microsoft\u2019s flagship operating system to create Windows 8, which was released in October.  Windows 8  While the new software ushered in major technological advancements, it also aroused the ire of some longtime users. Still, Larson-Green has been a  rising star  at Microsoft. She joined the company in 1993 and became a vice president in the Office division in 2006.  As demand wanes for PCs, the July management shakeup sought to turn away from Microsoft\u2019s original focus on \u201cputting a PC on every desk in every home,\u201d Ballmer wrote in a memo at the time. PC shipments fell about 11 percent in the second quarter, for a record fifth straight quarter of declines, according to market research firms IDC and Gartner Inc.  \u2018Comprehensive Vision\u2019  \u201cBallmer did a very good job turning Microsoft from a bloated monstrosity into a much leaner and meaner machine over the last few years,\u201d said Microsoft investor  Michael Obuchowski , a portfolio manager at North Shore Asset Management LLC in Cold Spring Harbor, New York. \u201cHowever, despite the improved operations and much better quality of programming, Microsoft was severely lacking a comprehensive vision that would have allowed the company to stay ahead of the trends.\u201d  Microsoft also is trying to challenge  Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN)  and Google in cloud services as more customers opt for software that\u2019s run over the Web instead of installed on corporate machines. Cloud efforts that were scattered across several divisions were concentrated under two units in the reorganization.  Even with all the recent executive changes, there\u2019s no heir apparent, Obuchowski said.  \u201cThis is not going to be an easy search,\u201d he said. \u201cThe expectations are very high and I don\u2019t think Microsoft can afford to make a mistake here. (MSFT) \u2019s Windows Server with second-hand copies purchased from a broker called Preo Software AG.  The move was eased by a July ruling from the European Union\u2019s highest court paving the way for sales of previously owned software. Bauske had some experience in the matter, having bought second-hand copies of Microsoft Office and Adobe Photoshop in 2006 and 2007, when the legality of such deals was less clear.  \u201cWe\u2019ve had to be certain that the savings outweigh the legal risks,\u201d Bauske said. \u201cNow there\u2019s less reason to be concerned.\u201d  On July 3 the European Court of Justice  ruled  in a case brought by  Oracle Corp. (ORCL)  seeking to prevent Munich-based UsedSoft GmbH from reselling software licenses. The court said developers can\u2019t forbid resale of programs and updates downloaded from the Internet, expanding earlier case law permitting the sale of second-hand software delivered on disk.  \u201cSoftware vendors have every reason to worry,\u201d said  Ray Wang , chief executive officer of Constellation Research, a technology adviser whose client roster includes Microsoft and  Adobe Systems Inc. (ADBE)   Demand Triples  Companies spend $250 billion to $275 billion on  business software  annually, Wang estimates. The total potential value of programs that might find buyers could exceed $1 trillion, Wang said, though the market today is much smaller. In  Germany , one of the biggest markets, less than 100 million euros ($131 million) of corporate software was resold last year, according to traders.  UsedSoft, which had sales of about 5 million euros last year, has seen demand triple since the July decision, said Chief Executive Officer Peter Schneider. The verdict \u201cwill make the market explode,\u201d he said.  Also fueling the resale business is an injunction from a Hamburg court last month forbidding Microsoft from warning potential buyers of used programs that such deals were illegal unless the software maker approved them.  Chemical and pharmaceuticals company  Bayer AG (BAYN) , car-parts maker  Magna International Inc. (MG) , and German retailer Edeka Zentrale AG & Co. are among companies that have tapped the used software market, according to the customer reference lists on the resellers\u2019 websites.  Bayer, Magna  Bayer Business Services, Bayer\u2019s IT branch, says it is re- evaluating the use of second-hand software following the ECJ verdict. Magna declined to comment. Edeka didn\u2019t respond to requests for comment.  Trading used business software isn\u2019t quite as seamless as selling secondhand video games on eBay. Sellers contact companies like UsedSoft with the programs and number of licenses they want to sell. Buyers similarly contact brokers with requests for specific programs. If brokers have the licenses, they quote a price, typically 30 percent to 70 percent of the original cost. The buyer can then use the license information to download the program from the software maker\u2019s Website.  The intermediaries usually take a cut of about 30 percent of the deal, said Boris Voege, co-founder and sales chief at Preo. A notary\u2019s certification testifying that the programs have been deleted from the seller\u2019s computers is often required to complete a deal.  Since not all companies want the latest versions of programs, the process helps sellers monetize an asset that would otherwise be discarded.  Older Versions  \u201cWhen Microsoft introduced Office 2007, demand for Office 2003 was skyrocketing because companies were used to it,\u201d said Dirk Lynen, CEO of 2ndsoft GmbH, a used software broker in the German city of Aachen.  In the U.S., most software contracts forbid resale, and there haven\u2019t been any decisive challenges to such clauses in court, said Eben Moglen, a Columbia Law School professor and founder of the Software Freedom Law Center.  Still, American companies can tap the market via European subsidiaries. The European decision confirmed the rule across the region that a vendor\u2019s right to control what happens to software expires with the first sale, much as is the case with physical goods.  Maintenance Model  While the most commonly traded programs have been Microsoft\u2019s Windows and Office and Adobe\u2019s Photoshop, makers of specialized business software have also fought resellers. A Dusseldorf court ordered  SAP AG (SAP)  in 2009 to stop telling a prospective buyer it would violate the law by purchasing pre- owned licenses.  \u201cThis model is seen as very critical by SAP,\u201d SAP\u2019s chief financial officer, Werner Brandt, said on a July 24 conference call. \u201cWe do not want to see this second market of our licenses evolving.\u201d  Officials at Microsoft and Oracle declined to comment on used software.  The decision could also threaten the ability of software developers to sell servicing agreements for their programs, a high-margin business that they count on for long-term revenue. Maintenance companies such as Spinnaker Support LLC and Rimini Street Inc. are seeing growing sales of software maintenance contracts that don\u2019t include the programs\u2019 writers.  In 2010, Oracle filed a lawsuit in U.S. District Court in  Nevada  against Rimini Street, a Las Vegas company that provides software support. Oracle argues that Rimini\u2019s business violates Oracle\u2019s intellectual property. The case has yet to be resolved.  Software Bundles  The original vendors could counter the threat of resellers by offering software on a rental basis rather than selling it, said  Christian Czychowski , who specializes on copyright and media law at Boehmert & Boehmert.  They could also sell larger license packages, which would be tougher to trade because the European court ruled that such bundles cannot be broken up and sold piece by piece. While it may take years, Czychowski said, it\u2019s likely that software companies will ultimately deliver most of their programs as an ongoing service rather than a one-off sale.  \u201cIn the future we will market software less and less like a physical good,\u201d Czychowski said. \u201cInstead it will be sold like electricity, priced according to how much you use it. But they're discovering, as the drawn-out lawsuits over intellectual property play out, that owning the rights to old inventions may not be worth as much as actually inventing and selling new things. The tech world's fiery passion for patents in finally starting to simmer, Michel Combes, chief executive officer at Alcatel-Lucent, said last week. \"There's less hype in the patent area than two years ago, when new players were extremely keen to get as many patents as they could -- in the mobile space especially.\" The Franco-American company, based in Paris at the foot of the Eiffel tower, knows what innovation is worth. It owns Bell Labs, the Nobel Prize-winning telecoms research center credited with inventing the transistor, the laser, and crucial programming languages and operating systems that underlie many of today's gadgets. Alcatel-Lucent has been looking to license some of the 30,000 or so patents it owns and the 15,000 others pending approval. They cover everything from voice recognition to video conferencing. After an agreement with licensing syndicate RPX proved insufficient, Alcatel-Lucent began setting up its own structure to do licensing work internally, it said about a year ago. Still, the company  has yet to generate any significant revenue from patent licensing . The bidding wars for patents, which  tech companies were amassing  to defend themselves against intellectual-property suits, was short-lived. Google acquired Motorola Mobility for $12.5 billion in 2011 as part of a move to get its hands on 17,000 patents and 7,000 more that had been filed. The deal would strengthen Google's patent portfolio and help it \"protect Android from anti-competitive threats from Microsoft, Apple and other companies,\" CEO Larry Page said then. A group of tech giants, including Apple, BlackBerry, Microsoft and Sony, outbid Google earlier that year for  Nortel Networks' portfolio of more than 6,000 patents . The price was a whopping $4.5 billion -- just for the patents, mind you. \"Since 2011, we haven't seen any transaction that size in the industry,\" said Yann Magnan, managing director at Duff & Phelps, which helps clients evaluate intangible assets. Last year,  AOL sold some patents  and began licensing others to Microsoft in a deal valued at $1.06 billion.  Facebook joined in by paying $550 million  for some of Microsoft's newly acquired patents. These were among the last blockbuster patent deals in the tech industry. PricewaterhouseCoopers called 2012  a \"banner year\" for patent-infringement litigation . Apple v. Samsung Electronics, Oracle v. Google, Yahoo! v. Facebook, and so on. The  Apple-Samsung showdown  has been a sloppy fight. During about a year of courtroom flip-flopping, Apple went from winning $1.05 billion in damages owed by Samsung to the threat of having some of its products banned from being sold. The Obama administration swooped in over the weekend to overturn the U.S. import ban. The case, along with other recent high-profile lawsuits, demonstrates that the murky patent-litigation process may be more trouble than it's worth for tech companies.","path":".\/2008_2012_msft_bloomberg_news\/ech-s-world-war-over-patents-is-cooling-off.txt"},{"id":25829198,"title":"Apple v Samsung: Can Look and Feel Be Patented?","released_at":"<date>August 1 2012<\/date> <time>04:01:01<\/time>","content":"Get ready for \u201crubberbanding.\u201d\nThat\u2019s the way the screen on an iPad or iPhone seems to bounce\nwhen you scroll to the bottom of a file -- and it\u2019s among the\nterms jurors must understand as  Apple Inc. Apple has become the most valuable company by creating\nproducts that stand out for design and ease of use, stemming\nfrom scores of smaller innovations, such as rubberbanding,\nrather than epic underlying technology breakthroughs. If Apple\nwere to win, Samsung could be forced to scale back features in\nits handsets, making them less attractive to consumers.  A victory could also help Apple hobble another important\nfoe: Android, the operating system that Google Inc. gives away\nto manufacturers and Samsung uses on key products. Google\u2019s\napproach threatens Apple\u2019s pitch to consumers that its exclusive\nofferings are different and better.  Engineering Patents  Courts historically have given greater protection to\nengineering-based innovations that create an entirely new way of\naccomplishing a task, said Milone, who practiced as a patent\nattorney before founding Article One. If granted, these so-\ncalled utility patents protect the inventor from copying for 20\nyears after the first filing.  Apple alleges that Samsung has infringed three such\npatents. One is for rubberbanding, and another relates to how\nusers can double-tap a Web page or photo to zoom in.  What sets Apple\u2019s case apart is the company\u2019s focus on\nprotecting design patents, which relate to the look and feel of\nits mobile products. The four in the  San Jose  trial cover such\nthings as the placement of the on-off button on the iPad and\niPhone and the devices\u2019 flat, edge-to-edge glass fronts. One of\nthe patent documents consists of little more than nine drawings\nof a rectangular tablet, with no dimensions.  Subjective Opinions  Design patents  carry  a term of 14 years and are often\nharder to defend than engineering patents because cases often\nhinge on more subjective opinions. Also, companies can often\nmake relatively easy cosmetic changes to their products to avoid\ninfringement.  In a countersuit being heard in the same case, Samsung\nclaims that Apple is infringing five patents, including two that\ninvolve basic telecommunications technology that let mobile\nphones talk to each other.  Apple\u2019s patent portfolio shows the weight the company puts\non design-based innovations. While just 2.7 percent of patents\ngranted to technology companies are design patents, 13.4 percent\nof Apple\u2019s 5,452 patents fall into this category, according to\n MDB Capital Group LLC , which maintains a patent database. Of the\n359 patents listing Apple\u2019s late co-Founder  Steve Jobs  as an\ninventor, 86 percent are for design.  \u201cApple patents the things that they think make Apple\nspecial,\u201d said Bob Borchers, a venture capitalist who used to\nwork at Apple. \u201cThey focus on the consumer\u2019s experience.\u201d  Microsoft Prevails  The company\u2019s previous efforts to win protection for such\nadvances has been mixed. In 1992, Apple lost a copyright-\ninfringement suit aimed at preventing  Microsoft Corp. (MSFT)  from using\ngraphical features of the Macintosh in Windows. The setback\nopened the market to Windows machines from companies such as\n Dell Inc. (DELL)  and  Hewlett-Packard Co. (HPQ)   When Apple introduced the iPhone in 2007, Jobs said his\ncompany filed for 200 patents to protect the invention. Apple\nhas been aggressive in asserting those, and has won bans on\nsales of versions of Samsung\u2019s Galaxy tablet in  Australia  and\nthe European Union. In the current trial, U.S. District Judge\nLucy Koh granted an injunction preventing sale of the tablet in\nthe U.S.  Apple is setting a high price for its patents in court.\nIt\u2019s asking for $2.5 billion, or as much as $7.5 billion if\njurors believe punitive damages are warranted.  Even $2.5 billion works out to about $31 for each device\nsold by Samsung. Apple ascribes $24 of that $31 to Samsung\u2019s\nmisuse of its design patents. In its countersuit, Samsung is\nasking Apple to pay $14 for each infringing device.  Apple\u2019s Challenge  As complicated as the case may be, Apple will try to\nconvince jurors of one essential idea: Its Korean rival is a\ncopycat. Samsung will contend that none of Apple\u2019s design\nflourishes are totally novel, and that offering patent\nprotection to the rectangular shape and flat front surface of\nits products would unfairly limit competition.  \u201cSamsung is on trial because it made a deliberate decision\nto copy Apple\u2019s iPhone and iPad,\u201d Apple said in the opening\nline of its key pretrial filing with the court. \u201cTry as it\nmight,\u201d Apple said, \u201cSamsung cannot deflect attention from its\nown copying by the patents it has asserted against Apple.\u201d  In its filing, Samsung answered that a lot of competing\nproducts appear similar.  \u201cIn this lawsuit,\u201d the company said, \u201cApple seeks to\nstifle legitimate competition and limit consumer choice to\nmaintain its historically exorbitant profits.\u201d  Hard Defense  Apple may have an advantage in that Koh is a former\nintellectual property lawyer who has been willing to consider\nthe company\u2019s argument. She granted the preliminary injunction\non Samsung\u2019s tablet, and hasn\u2019t referred to a recent ruling by\n Richard Posner , the federal judge who in June dismissed a suit\nbetween Apple and Google\u2019s Motorola Mobility because neither\ncould prove that it had been damaged economically.  To prevail in San Jose, Apple will need to persuade jurors\n-- and that won\u2019t be easy, even in a case being heard just a few\nmiles from its headquarters, said Kevin Rivette,  managing\npartner  at 3LP Advisors LLC and a former vice president of\nintellectual-property strategy for International Business\nMachines Corp.  \u201cDesign patents are supposed to be hard to defend,\u201d\nRivette said. \u201cIf you could stop everyone by patenting a\nrectangular phone, then Motorola could have done it years ago\nand none of this ever would have happened.\u201d  The case is Apple Inc. v. In both subjects, poor students, black children and those who speak English as a second language fared better in charters.  The study, one of the largest ever of charter school performance, buoyed advocates of the school-choice movement, which views charters as an alternative to the shortcomings of public education. Results from the study of 25 states and the  District of Columbia  represent a turnabout from a 2009 report that had shown charter schools children faring worse.  \u201cThe charter sector does seem to be posting better results, especially with disadvantaged students,\u201d said Margaret Raymond, director of Stanford\u2019s  Center for Research on Education Outcomes , which conducted the study. \u201cThe fact that they are moving the needle with this many students since 2009 is a pretty impressive finding.\u201d  The earlier report, which included 16 states, found that students at charters schools posted seven fewer days of learning in reading and 22 fewer in math a year relative to regular school peers.  Academic Quality  Charter schools  have grown more serious about academic quality because of the national debate about their effectiveness, Raymond said in a telephone interview. Higher expectations and parent involvement may also play a role, she said. Equally important, those overseeing charters have started shutting down poor performers, she said.  As many as one in five charter schools should be closed because of poor academic performance, according to a November 2012 report from the  National Association of Charter School Authorizers , which represents states, districts and universities that grant them permission to operate.  \u201cPolicy makers have to be willing to make the tough political call to say no to keeping a failing school open,\u201d said Greg Richmond, president and chief executive officer of the National Association of Charter School Authorizers in  Chicago . \u201cThere are still 1,000 schools that are worse than their counterparts. We need to recognize that fact and deal with it.\u201d  Teachers\u2019 Unions  Charter schools, which are run without many of the rules of regular public schools, typically don\u2019t have contracts with teachers\u2019 unions and often feature longer school days.  Business leaders such as  Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) \u2019s  Bill Gates , President  Barack Obama  and many Republicans including former Florida Governor Jeb Bush support charters. In  New York  City, Wall Street executives offer financial backing for growing chains of schools that include Knowledge Is Power Program, or KIPP, and Success Academy.  Critics, including some teachers\u2019 unions, say charters skim off students from the most committed families and siphon money and resources from regular schools. Parents of students with disabilities have said some charters exclude their children. The Stanford study found that charters have a lower proportion of special-education students than other schools.  \u201cWe should ask ourselves why we keep pitting charter schools against neighborhood public schools -- a strategy that has created little more than a disruptive churn,\u201d  Randi Weingarten , president of the  American Federation of Teachers , said in a statement, adding that the performance difference is negligible.  Unequal Benefits  Students from all backgrounds didn\u2019t benefit equally from charter schools, the study found. Black students in poverty achieved above-average learning gains -- equivalent to 36 additional days of learning in math -- as did low-income Hispanic students. White students fared worse overall, while Asians did more poorly only in math.  To address concerns about differences in school populations, the Stanford study sought to compare the improvement in academic achievement of similar students, matching each pupil at a charter with a \u201cvirtual twin\u201d at a regular school with similar state test scores while controlling for demographics.  Charters now serve about 4 percent of the nation\u2019s public school pupils, with more than 2.3 million students in over 6,000 schools in 41 states, according to the study. Enrollment has surged 80 percent since the 2009 report.  Charter Gains  In the study, 25 percent of charter schools showed significantly stronger learning gains in reading than traditional schools, while 56 percent showed no real difference and 19 percent of charters lagged. In math, 29 percent of charter schools outperformed, while 40 percent were about the same and 31 percent were weaker.  The study found wide varieties among charters schools in different states.  Rhode Island \u2019s charter schools showed among the biggest gains relative to regular public schools -- equivalent to 85 days in reading and 111 in math.  In the District of Columbia and  New York City , which was broken out separately, charters also outperformed by a wide margin. New York City charter school children learned an additional 92 days of math in a year.  Education Reforms  \u201cIf there\u2019s one thing this report confirms, it\u2019s that we can\u2019t roll back the reforms that have transformed the educational landscape in New York,\u201d said Devon Puglia, deputy press secretary for the city\u2019s education department.  Nevada charters had far worse results than regular schools in reading and math -- equal to 139 fewer days of learning. Pennsylvania charters also underperformed. Steven Canavero, a spokesman for the Nevada Education Department, said the state has already taken steps to address underperforming schools.  \u201cThis report affirms what we already knew,\u201d Canavero said in a phone interview. \u201cWe have established new expectations for schools and provided standards so now it\u2019s about implementation.\u201d  Some education researchers criticized the study\u2019s claims. The data from the report show no significant difference between charters and traditional schools, according to Andrew Maul, a researcher at the National Education Policy Center and a professor at the  University of Colorado  in Boulder.  ``It\u2019s incredibly small, and therefore it\u2019s basically a zero finding.\u201d Maul said in a telephone interview. The correct answer could be lucrative. Research firm IDC estimates that India's share of the global smartphone market will grow from 3 percent today to 10 percent in 2017, when some 1.5 billion units are expected to ship around the world. That would make the country the No. 3 market behind China and the U.S. India is currently ranked sixth. \u201cIt is important to understand the Indian economic pyramid,\u201d Ravi Venkatesan, the former chairman of Microsoft India, said in an interview on Bloomberg Radio. \u201cThe big economic opportunity is in the middle, but it is a very, very hard market to crack.\" He explained that mobile companies need to drastically change their approach to these consumers. \"So what you need to do is come up with stuff that is dramatically more affordable -- think: smartphones at $50, cell phone calls at 1 cent a minute,\" Venkatesan said. \"And that takes innovation.\u201d Samsung Electronics and Apple, the world\u2019s top two smartphone makers, have very different approaches to emerging markets such as India. Samsung makes a wide variety of Android-based models, from the low end to the flagship Galaxy S4. That has helped the Korean electronics giant become the top smartphone maker in India in the last quarter of 2012, according to IDC. On the other hand, Apple releases one new model of the iPhone a year, and the latest is always top-of-the-line. (AMZN)  Chief Executive Officer  Jeff Bezos , who is betting he can apply his success in e-commerce to the struggling newspaper industry.  Bezos is making the deal as an individual and not as part of Amazon, the world\u2019s biggest online retailer, according to a statement yesterday. Current owner Washington Post Co., which isn\u2019t selling its Kaplan education division and other businesses as part of the transaction, now plans to change its name.  In acquiring the publication, famed for its coverage of the 1970s Watergate scandal that led to the only resignation of a U.S. president, Bezos becomes the latest billionaire to try his hand at reviving the newspaper business. Boston  Red Sox  owner  John Henry  agreed to buy the Boston Globe last week, and Warren Buffett assembled an empire of community papers in recent years.  \u201cI understand the critical role the Post plays in Washington, D.C., and our nation, and the Post\u2019s values will not change,\u201d Bezos said in the statement. \u201cOur duty to readers will continue to be the heart of the Post, and I am very optimistic about the future.\u201d  Eight Decades  The deal marks the end of the paper\u2019s stewardship by the Graham family and its relatives, who acquired the Post in 1933.  It was on their watch that newspaper covered a 1972 break-in at the Democratic National Headquarters at Washington\u2019s Watergate complex and subsequent cover-up, eventually leading President  Richard Nixon  to resign. The film \u201cAll the President\u2019s Men\u201d chronicled the events and enshrined the Post\u2019s mysterious source -- \u201cDeep Throat\u201d -- in popular culture. Reporters  Bob Woodward  and Carl Bernstein protected their source, FBI agent W. Mark Felt, until Felt revealed his identity in  Vanity Fair  in May 2005.  Seven years of declining sales, triggered by an industrywide advertising slump, ultimately pushed the family to sell. Investment bank Allen & Co. handled the process.  \u201cThis is a day that my family and I never expected to come,\u201d Publisher Katharine Weymouth, niece of Chairman Don Graham, said in a letter to readers. \u201cThe Washington Post Co. is selling the newspaper it has owned and nurtured for eight decades.\u201d  \u2018Threw in Towel\u2019  Washington Post Co., which also owns Post- Newsweek  Stations and Cable ONE, hasn\u2019t announced what its new name will be. The stock has gained 62 percent this year.  Washington Post Co.\u2019s newspaper division reported widening operating losses in the past two years, including a $53.7 million loss in 2012, according to its annual filings. The division\u2019s annual sales declined 7 percent to $581.7 million in 2012, with the Washington Post\u2019s print advertising, once the lifeblood of the paper, falling 14 percent to $228.2 million in the same period.  Pension Payments  As part of the agreement, Bezos will take on the pension obligations of  current employees  while Washington Post Co. will handle retired workers. The company also will provide Bezos with $50 million to help pay the obligations. The sale proceeds will go to the Washington Post Co., rather than the Graham family directly.  In a May filing, Washington Post Co. had valued its newspaper-publishing division at $255.6 million -- within $6 million of Bezos\u2019s purchase price. That\u2019s less than 10 percent of the company\u2019s $4.4 billion market value.  The transaction extends a frenzy of media deals over the past four days. On Aug. 3,  New York Times Co. (NYT)  announced plans to sell the Boston Globe to Henry, a billionaire hedge-fund manager who owns the Red Sox and the Liverpool Football Club. Bezos\u2019s Wealth  Bezos, 49, has a net worth of $27.9 billion, making him No. 16 on the  Bloomberg Billionaires Index . He ranks above Google Inc. co-founders  Larry Page  and  Sergey Brin , as well as Microsoft CEO  Steve Ballmer  and  Dell Inc. (DELL)  founder  Michael Dell .  Over the past three months, Bezos\u2019s 86.4 million Amazon shares have increased or decreased in value each day by an average of $249 million -- almost the same as the price he\u2019s paying for the newspaper.  Most of Bezos\u2019s fortune is tied to a 19 percent stake in Amazon. Since the company\u2019s initial public offering in 1995, Bezos has sold almost $2 billion in Amazon stock. Much of that has been plowed into Blue Origin, his closely held space-exploration company.  After deducting $175 million in Blue Origin funding, Bezos probably has about $1.7 billion in cash and other investable assets, based on an analysis of insider transactions, dividend income, taxes and market performance.  \u2018Day Job\u2019  Bezos made an earlier foray into the media business in April, when he participated in a $5 million investment round for Business Insider Inc., the news site co-founded by  Henry Blodget , the former Internet industry analyst. The Amazon founder\u2019s Bezos Expeditions investment firm handled the investment.  Bezos said he would keep the Post\u2019s current management in place while he remains in  Seattle  focusing on Amazon. Weymouth will stay on as publisher and CEO.  \u201cI am happily living in \u2018the other Washington\u2019 where I have a day job that I love,\u201d Bezos said. \u201cThe Post already has an excellent leadership team that knows much more about the news business than I do, and I\u2019m extremely grateful to them for agreeing to stay on.\u201d  Following Buffett  While he won\u2019t be moving to the capital, Bezos has taken an interest in politics before. He and his wife, MacKenzie, made a $2.5 million  donation  to a Washington campaign to defend the state\u2019s law protecting same-sex marriage last year. He also has supported the creation of a federal framework for collecting sales tax online.  Drew Herdener, a spokesman for Bezos, declined to comment beyond the public statements.  In tackling the newspaper industry, Bezos is following in the footsteps of Buffett, who has his own connection to the Post. Buffett served on the board of Washington Post Co. until 2011 and his company, Berkshire Hathaway Inc., is the Post\u2019s largest shareholder -- an investment he pledged to keep the year he resigned as a director. Buffett didn\u2019t respond to a request for comment sent to an assistant yesterday.  Berkshire held 1.73 million Washington Post shares as of July 17, according to a regulatory filing. If unaltered, that stake climbed by more than $40 million today. Buffett has said in letters to investors that he purchased the shares for about $10 million in 1973. Community Papers  Berkshire has been expanding its newspaper operations in the past two years, buying publications in towns with a strong sense of community, rather than in large cities with more competition among news providers. Net income in the period that ended Sept. 30 rose to $5.24 billion, or 62 cents a share, from $4.47 billion, or 53 cents, a year earlier, Microsoft said today in a statement. Sales climbed 16 percent to $18.5 billion. Analysts on average had predicted profit of 54 cents on $17.8 billion in revenue, according to  data  compiled by Bloomberg. The shares jumped in late trading.  The world\u2019s largest software maker is undergoing unprecedented changes, conducting its first-ever CEO search and starting an organizational overhaul aimed at bolstering sales by focusing on devices and services. Demand for Microsoft\u2019s Office productivity software has helped compensate for declining consumer purchases of PCs running Windows, and the company has been cutting costs to shore up profit.  \u201cBusiness has been driving the train,\u201d said  Colin Gillis , an analyst at BGC Partners LP in New York, who recommends holding the shares. \u201cMost people are really looking through the quarter to the new CEO.\u201d  Microsoft shares rose as much as 7.4 percent to $36.21 in extended trading following the report. Corporate Sales  For the current quarter, Redmond, Washington-based Microsoft forecast higher sales of its commercial products and services, which includes corporate sales of Office and server software, as well strong Xbox demand as a new game console is rolled out. While the company didn\u2019t provide a projection for total revenue, at the low end of the ranges provided for each of five divisions, sales for the fiscal second quarter would exceed the $22.9 billion average estimate of analysts polled by Bloomberg.  Microsoft\u2019s first-quarter revenue got a lift from products like the SQL database server, SharePoint, Exchange for e-mail, and Lync for corporate messaging and telephony. Revenue from commercial cloud products more than doubled.  In the commercial division, which includes these corporate products, licensing revenue jumped 7.3 percent to $9.59 billion, and other corporate revenue, including Internet cloud-based programs, rose to $1.6 billion. That compares with average analysts\u2019 estimates of $9.42 billion and $1.58 billion, respectively, based on four estimates compiled by Bloomberg.  Future Revenue  Unearned revenue, which comes from sales of multiyear deals that will be recognized in the future, was $20.2 billion for the quarter, compared with the $21.1 billion average  analyst  projection, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.  Consumer demand for PCs wasn\u2019t as bad as Microsoft had expected, particularly in developed markets, and corporate PC sales are showing signs of stabilizing, Chief Financial Officer  Amy Hood  said in an interview. PC sales in China continue to be weak because of excess inventory. Similar trends should persist in the current quarter, she said.  \u201cI thought this was going to be a quiet quarter because we are waiting to see what Surface 2 does at holiday, and waiting for a new CEO, Windows 8 traction and all these things, but it was a very strong quarter,\u201d said  Daniel Morgan , a fund manager at Synovus Trust Co. in Atlanta, which owns Microsoft shares. Goldman Sachs Group Inc. had estimated the devices and their accessories would pull in $181 million in sales. Other commercial revenue, which includes the company\u2019s corporate cloud programs, will be $1.7 billion to $1.9 billion, she projected.  In the consumer and devices unit, licensing sales will be $5.2 billion to $5.4 billion; revenue from hardware, which includes the new Xbox, will be $3.8 billion to $4.1 billion; and other consumer products will bring in $1.7 billion to $1.8 billion, she said.  The software maker\u2019s sales growth had been hurt in recent quarters as the PC market contracted amid a transition to mobile devices for surfing the Internet. Worldwide PC shipments fell 8.6 percent last quarter, researcher Gartner Inc. said earlier this month, amid lackluster demand from students returning to school.  Mobile Push  Microsoft\u2019s efforts in mobile phones and tablets have produced little progress in what is already an uphill climb to keep Apple Inc.\u2019s iOS and Google Inc.\u2019s Android operating system from shutting out Windows. Three years after rejiggering its phone software to be more appealing to consumers, Microsoft still has only  3.7 percent  share in smartphone operating systems, according to IDC. Its  share  in tablets in the second quarter came in at 4.5 percent for all versions of Windows, IDC said.  In July, the company\u2019s profit in the fiscal fourth quarter missed projections by the the biggest margin in at least 10 years. Results also were hurt by a $900 million writedown of inventory of Surface tablets. The company cut prices for the devices, which first went on sale a year ago, to clear inventory ahead of the introduction of updated models this week.  Ballmer\u2019s Departure  A week before the fourth-quarter earnings miss, Ballmer unveiled Microsoft\u2019s biggest management shuffle in more than a decade, a bid to align the company around hardware and Internet-based services and an attempt to halt the slide of Windows.  Then, in August, the company said that Ballmer, who took over as CEO from co-founder  Bill Gates  in 2000, will step down from that role within a year. People with knowledge of the matter said earlier this month that the board is aiming to have a successor in place by the end of 2013.  To reinforce its efforts in mobile, Microsoft reached an agreement in September to acquire Nokia Oyj\u2019s handset unit for $7.2 billion. Windows Phone\u2019s third-place ranking in smartphone operating systems in the second quarter compared with 79 percent market share for Google\u2019s Android and 13 percent for  Apple \u2019s iOS, IDC said in August.  Following the July business reorganization, Microsoft altered how it reports revenue from different units, opting for a structure that splits sales into a total of five segments and provides operating income for two larger categories: one for commercial business, such as Windows and Office corporate software licenses and services; and the other for devices and consumer products, including Xbox, Surface, consumer Windows sales and its Bing search engine. Only a quarter of people in developing countries are\nonline, compared with three-quarters in developed nations. Kenya\u2019s Internet  Kenya has some of the fastest, cheapest Internet access in\nAfrica thanks to government investment in technology, low taxes\non hardware and software, and policies discouraging\ncommunications monopolies. Chang spends her time teaming up\ndiplomats with U.S. technology companies and nonprofit groups to\nfigure out how other countries can follow Kenya\u2019s example. Scarce Hubs  In the U.S. there are dozens of these hubs; Kenya has at\nleast one. Web traffic from these nations must travel over\ninternational fiber-optic cables to hubs hundreds or thousands\nof miles away, slowing service and driving up costs. The\nAlliance is seeking to use corporate and diplomatic power to\npush governments to change laws getting in the way of Internet\naccess.
